newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rejects "laughable" U.S. anti-drugs money.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rejects "laughable" U.S. anti-drugs money.

text.p: Brazil has rejected a $600,000 offer from the United States to help in its anti-drugs war because Brasilia considered the sum "laughable", officials said on Tuesday.
A spokeswoman said Justice Minister Nelson Jobim had decided over the weekend to reject the funds from Washington's Drug Enforcement Agency (DEA), offered to Brazil for 1997.
"Minister Jobim ordered the money be rejected," she said.
Newspapers and officials said Jobim considered the $600,000 "laughable".
No one was immediately available for comment at the U.S. embassy in Brasilia.
Newspapers reported that Jobim's decision was supported by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso.
They added it had taken U.S. officials by surprise and strained relations between the two capitals.
O Globo newspaper said Jobim had halted talks with the DEA over cooperation in the drugs war. "There's no point in talking over this amount of money," Globo quoted him as saying.

Officials said that last year, the DEA gave $20 million to Colombia. They said that Brazil, as a major transhipment route if not producer of cocaine from Bolivia, Peru and Colombia, should be given similar assistance.
"We are no longer going to follow the DEA policy of erecting a wall only to prevent drugs entering the United States without caring for the countries through which the drugs pass," Jobim told Globo.
